FOREST CONSERVATION, DEVELOPMENT AND REGENERATION
Recommendation
The Committee was given to  understand that one of the goals of the Ministry is to increase the forest cover of the
 country upto 25%  by 2007  and 33% by 2012. The Committee appreciates the goal set out by the Ministry but is of the view
 that a blanket approach should not be adopted in this regard. Some States already have a forest cover in excess of 33% and
 complain about hampering of development activities due to thick forest cover. Therefore, the policy of increasing forest cover
 should be implemented only in those states which are short of the stipulated target so that a balanced proportion of forest cover 
 can be maintained in all parts of the country.
(Para 55)
 
Action taken by the Ministry
This recommendation of the Committee has a policy dimension.  As far as Ministry is concerned it is clarified that the
 afforestation programame is being taken up only in the degraded forest areas and fringe villages.  Therefore the quality of the
 forest and in turn the forest is being improved within the recorded forest area only, which otherwise cannot be diverted for
 development works without the approval of the competent authority under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.
            The productive and protective nature of forests transcends geographical boundaries.  In order to maintain this nature of
 forests, one of the most important goals of the Ministry is to increase the forest cover of the country upto 25% by 2007 and 33%
 by 2012.  The developmental activities in any state are not hampered because of the thick forest cover.  The diversion of forest
 land for non-forestry activities under Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, for various developmental projects like Power,
 Irrigation, Drinking water supply, Roads, Railway Lines etc. is considered on the merits of the case. India is committed to the
 concept of sustainable management of its forest resources and tree wealth.  The proportion of the country’s geographical area
 under forest/tree cover is one of the basic criteria to judge sustainability. The National Forest Policy, 1988 envisages that
 national goal should be to have a minimum of one third of total land area of the country under forest/tree cover. In the hills and
 in the mountainous region, the aim should be to maintain two third of the area under such cover in order to prevent erosion and
 land degradation and ensure the stability of the fragile ecosystem.
            Forest is on the Concurrent List of the Constitution. It is true that the forest cover in some of the states is more than
 national goal, but the national goal has not been achieved so far. The Ministry of Environment & Forests is trying to achieve the
 national goal enshrined in the National Forest Policy, 1988 in a holistic way with a full support to the forest rich states by
 assisting them in strengthening the institutional framework like Joint Forest Management Committees, Forest Development
 Agencies and funding through various centrally sponsored schemes. Simultaneously, efforts are being made on promoting tree
 plantation both outside and inside the forest areas in those states which are deficient in forest/tree cover.  The efforts are being
 made on both the forest rich and deficient states, as we have to take a holistic picture at the national level. While the focus has

NATIONAL LAKE CONSERVATION PLAN
Recommendation
The Committee is  perturbed to note that a big project which could play a significant role in restoring the environmental
 health of the country is suffering due to apathy and the lackadaisical attitude of the Central and State Governments. It was
 started in 1994, but little seems to have been done for cleaning of lakes and a lot of  time has been spent either in finalizing
 contracts or preparing action plans or discussing cost factors.  The Committee feels that lakes are critical in sustaining the
 environmental health of our cities. Acting as a huge reservoir, they not only provide water but also recharge and replenish the
 ground water. Lakes also play an important role in preventing floods. Besides, their importance from the point of view of
 beauty, and aesthetics are well acclaimed. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry come out with a
 comprehensive approach and execute all its programmes with seriousness and commitment. Otherwise our lakes will very soon
 be garbage dumps. When lakes dry up during continuous droughts like in Rajasthan today it is suggested that programme for
 desilting and deepening of the bed of those lakes needs to be taken up on a war footing, if necessary with the help of Army
 Engineering Corps.
(Para 64)
Action taken by the Ministry
            The National Lake Conservation Plan (NLCP) was conceptualized in 1994.  After obtaining the pre-feasibility reports
 from the State Governments for 10 identified lakes, the NLCP was posed for approval  by the Cabinet Committee.  The
 Ministry was however, directed to seek external assistance.  No external funding agency evinced any interest.  The Government
 of  India’s approval to lake conservation was accorded in June, 2001.  Since then 22 lakes have already been approved for
 taking up conservation measure at an estimated cost of  about  Rs. 137 crore.  So far an expenditure of Rs.1.90 crore has been
 incurred on NLCP.  The site specific conservation measures include sewage diversion and treatment, desilting, deweeding,
 insitu lake conservation measures like bioremediation on constructed wetland, lake beautification and lake front development,
 low cost sanitation, public participation etc.
The scope of work under NLCP has been enlarged during the X Plan by including conservation of rural lakes along with
 urban lakes.  All State Governments have been asked to prioritise and send proposals for lakes in their States.  Depending upon
 the pollution status and the availability of funds, these shall be included under NLCP.  During the last meeting of  NRCA held

BIO-MEDICAL WASTE MANAGEMENT
Recommendation
      The Committee feels that the scientific management of medical waste is being  dangerously neglected in the country. The
 staff charged with the responsibility for sanitation and cleanliness in hospitals and other medical units seem to be ignorant of
 the regulations for Bio-medical waste (BMW) disposal. Hoards of broken needles, soiled cotton  and bandages, laboratory
 tested blood/urine/stood samples, leftover plaster of Paris coats, abandoned organs, used utensils, instruments and containers
 lying right in the precincts of hospitals have been noticed by people. Even these wastes have been shown to the M.Ps. The
 Committee observes that in some parts of the country many incinerators installed to dispose of medical waste are dysfunctional.
 In U.P. alone out of 33 incinerators, 31 are not functioning. The Committee recommends that responsibility has to be fixed for
 the negligence which cause such a state of affairs and deterrent action taken against the officers responsible for the running of
 incinerators. The Committee, therefore, recommends that  persons in small and big nursing homes and all hospitals heed to be
 trained regarding this aspect. A  capsule one or two day course  should be run each month in all leading Government hospitals
 of the country and not only staff but the hospital  in-charge must also be  made to attend these courses at the end of which
 proper certificate should also be awarded  to trainees. Taking into account the mushrooming growth of nursing homes the
 Committee recommends that a proposal may  be considered to link the opening of nursing homes with their capacity to treat
 and manage biomedical wastes. Medical waste management cannot be left only to the Municipalities. Open discussions should
 also be held among technical experts people’s  representatives and representatives of hospitals and nursing homes for evolving
 a strategy and method for proper disposal of BMW. In addition to these measures, a recycling industry bases on hospital waste
 needs to be dealt with in an exemplary fashion.

 population, professionals and the general public are covered under NEAC. More than 8,000 organisations participated in the
 campaign in 2002-03 covering almost all the districts in the country.
National Green Corps (Eco-clubs)
The main objectives of this programme are to educate children about their immediate environment and impart
 knowledge about the eco-systems, their inter-dependence and their fragile balance.     This   awareness  is created through visits
 tonature sites and to mobilize youngsters by instilling in them the spirit of scientific inquiry into environmental  problems and
 involving them in the efforts of environmental preservation.
A programme of raising “National Green Corps” through the Eco clubs was, therefore, lunched during 2001-2002.
 Under this programme, Eco-clubs are set up in 100  schools in each District of the country .More then 50,000 Eco-clubs have
 been set up so far in the country. This programme is being implemented in all the States/UTs the State/UT Govt.  The
 Government of India provides financial assistance for establishment of Eco clubs @ Rs.1000 per Eco-club. It also assists the
 States for teacher training and resource materials.

 teachers and school children.   In the context of orders of the Supreme Court to make environmental education compulsory for
 students in schools and colleges, the Ministry may find it useful to take such a step.

Recommendation
For effective implementation of the policies and programmes of the Ministry the Committee feels that instead of
 bureaucrats more and more technocrats and scientists should be associated.

The Ministry has a balanced composition of bureaucrats, technocrats, and scientists.  The manpower in subordinate
 offices of the Central Pollution Control Board, Botanical Survey of India, Zoological Survey of India is pre-dominantly
 scientific and technical with a miniscule of non-scientific personnel in Group ‘A’ category of posts.

 and administrators with long-term vision, and ability to synthesise and synergise on the one hand ,  and scientists and
 technocrats with scientific and technical expertise on the other hand.  The number of scientists, technocrats, and Indian Forest
 Service Officers taken together on the posts in the range of Secretary to Under Secretary is far in excess of policy-makers,
 planners and administrators.

The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Biotechnology on the Recommendations

 Hundred- sixteenth Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the Recommendations of the Committee were received
 from the Department on 30
th July, 2003.
The Committee’s Recommendation, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the action taken by the
 Department of Scientific and Industrial Research are set out in the succeeding paragraphs: -
Recommendation
            The Committee was informed that one of the recurring problems of the Department is the shortfall of the non-plan
 budget.  Recurrence of such problems on year to year basis, the committee was apprised, has created a compelling situation for
 the autonomous bodies whereby they had to cut down from plan funds to pay salaries to the scientists.  The Committee is
 constrained to note that scientific institutions engaged in research in frontier areas of science have to confront such a situation. 
 The additional requirement of the Department of non-plan expenditure is to the tune of Rs.5.00 crores.  The Committee,
 therefore, recommends that sufficient funds may be provided to the Department to overcome this problem.  It further underlines
 that the Departments dealing with science and technology should be accorded priority for allocation of funds and if necessary,
 special provisions may be made for them so that they do not face such problems.  Biotechnology era is waiting to dominate the
 World economy in the next twenty years.  Investment in this field is not commensurate with the potential of this branch of
 Science.
(Para 8)
Action taken by the Department
The Department has corresponded with Ministry of Finance, Government of India, on additional non-plan requirement as
 per recommendations. The matter is being pursued.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Department will pursue the Ministry of Finance to take cognizance of
 the matter.

Recommendation
The Committee recommends the Department to accord high priority to the issue of Human Resource Development and
 should coordinate with the University Grants Commission to implement the programme all over the country.

The Human Resource Development programme has been accorded high priority by the department. The department has
 decided to start new courses in the specialized subject areas of biotechnology in different parts of the country. For the first time
 model syllabi has been published for the post graduate courses in general biotechnology, medical biotechnology, agriculture
 biotechnology, animal biotechnology and M.Tech in biochemical engineering and biotechnology and circulated to University
 Grant Commission (UGC), Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD), All India Council for Technical Education
 (AICTE), Universities/ institutions who are implementing post graduate teaching courses supported by the department as well
 as other universities for implementation from the academic session 2003-04. It is also proposed to start Ph. D fellowship

Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that efforts should be made to make use of the tissue culture and floriculture technology in
 rural area.  Additional incentives should be given to persons willing to work in these areas.
(Para 20)
Action taken by the Department
            Department of Biotechnology has been supporting the area of plant tissue culture through a number of R&D projects and
 large-scale production facilities.  The two Micropropagation Technology Parks supported by DBT along with the six Regional
 Hardening Units in different parts of the country are making a concerted effort to promote this technology for application at the
 grass root level.  There is an enormous domestic market potential and efforts are being made to demonstrate the feasibility of this
 technology to farmers and other end users so as to take up this technology on a large scale.  Micropropagation technologies have
 been standardized for a large number of forest trees, horticulture and other economically important crops.  Demonstrations have
 been organized for agro forestry and agriculture sector through the help of state departments, corporations, NGOs and other
 extension agencies.
            A Consortium on Micropropagation Research and Development has now been established and programme support is
 being provided specifically for socio-economic development.  Different sites have been identified in the states of Maharashtra,
 Haryana and Punjab where grass root rural workers are being given extensive training.  Training is also provided through the
 National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) and Small Farmers Agri Consortium (SFAC) sponsored
 programmes on agro techniques and agri business ventures.  This is mainly for the educated youth who wish to take up
 agriculture as an enterprise. 
            The demonstration plots established in the agro forestry sector have yielded very good results at the farmer’s field in
 association with the Agro Forestry federation.  42% higher net profit has been achieved in the case of Eucalyptus and this
 technology has now been taken up by a commercial firm to cater to the needs of the farmers.
            Another important activity is training of the farmers through the Joint Forestry Management projects especially in the
 state of Haryana.  Special training programmes have been organized for potato and sugarcane, since, both these crops have a
 large demand.
            Special initiative has been taken by the Department was for rehabilitation of the Earthquake victims  of Gujrat in Bhuj. 
 Under a project coordinated by the Science Ashram, Baroda a green house has been established in collaboration with one of the
 local NGOs for producing vegetables all year round.  This has been very successful and an increase in the income specially of
 women has been noted.  Large-scale plantation of important forest trees such as Bamboo and Salvadora has also been initiated
 for the afforestation programme.  Bamboo plantation has been promoted in this region which would ultimately lead to socio-
economic upliftment of the people. 
            Application of tissue culture for floriculture is also being promoted through the DBT supported programmes specially for
 large scale production of important flowering and non-flowering plants which will lead to direct income generation.  A
 coordinated programme on orchids is now being evolved which would help in developing important novel varieties for large
 scale multiplication to cater to the domestic and export market.

The Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Department in vaccine research and development.  The Committee

In the medical biotechnology and health-care areas, the Department has major emphasis towards development of suitable

 undergoing preclinical animal experimentations and likely to enter human clinical trials after successful completion of the same.
 The DNA Rabies Vaccine for animals is likely to be available in near future. Current programmes either have been initiated or
 being initiated to study the microbial genomics as the information will be useful towards better understanding of the
 microorganisms, development of diagnostics and vaccines including the disease process and pathogenesis. During the current
 financial year, the Department has emphasis towards development of new multicentric interactive programmes on respiratory
 diseases, leishmaniasis and cardiovascular diseases/disorders. As a policy matter, it is intended to keep the cost of the
 vaccines/diagnostics within the reasonable and affordable limit so that they can be available to the common people. This aspect
 has always been taken into consideration while negotiating with the industries towards commercialization. However, the
 marketing is done by the Industry, thus only efforts can be made. Final price will depend upon industries own marketing
 strategy.
Comments
The Committee commends the endeavour by the Department towards development assay systems for the quick and
 accurate diagnosis of major diseases and various programmes initiated to study different diseases.  The Committee would like to
 see more such steps to be taken to make it affordable to common people.
BIO-TECHNOLOGY FOR SOCIETAL DEVELOPMENT
Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that the farmers and other needy people from the target groups should be provided with
 latest biotechnologies for mushroom cultivation and vermi-composting.  The committee notes with satisfaction that the
 Department has started approaching the State Governments for getting their support for production of biofertilizer.  While it is

 important for the Department to augment their efforts in this regard the Committee recommends that small and medium
 enterprises and industries may also be approached for this purpose.
(Para 34)
Action taken by the Department
Department is implementing projects for the benefit of SC/ST, rural and women population through training and
 demonstration of various biotechnological products and processes. Projects are also being implemented on different aspects of
 vermicomposting and mushroom cultivation.  At present projects are in progress on vermicomposting at Alwar, Tonk, Jaipur,
 Jhalawar, Kota & Baran districts of Rajasthan and certain places of Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh.
 Projects for imparting training and popularizing cultivation of mushroom have been commissioned at places like Jabalpur,
 Ujjain and Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh; Neempith, Hasnabad, Hoogly, Burdwan, Siliguri and Kancharapara in West Bengal;
 Salem, Madurai, Virudhunagar and Dindigul in Tamil Nadu; Trivandrum in Kerala, Imphal in Manipur and Parbani in
 Maharashtra.  Efforts are also being made to cover more and more areas under this programme. 
            Department has taken initiatives to popularize the application various biofertilisers and a number of packages specific to
 the cropping system prevalent to various agro climatic zones are being developed for Integrated Nutrient Management.  The
 package will be transferred to the Department of Agriculture & Cooperation (DAC), Ministry of Agriculture, Government of
 India for its large scale use. Department organized a number of entrepreneurs meet which were attended by large number of
 participants.  Efforts are also being made to transfer the technology packages developed by the department under this
 programme to small entrepreneurs.  The technology packages developed by the department have already been transferred to
 four entrepreneurs located at Ahmedabad, Vijaywada, Hyderabad, and Amrawati for large scale commercial production.  
Comments
The Committee appreciates the projects undertaken for the target groups and the efforts taken to popularize the
 application of biofertilizers.  The Committee is also of the view that more steps should be taken for the involvement of
 enterprises and industries.
Recommendation
The Committee also recommends that under the programme for women, emphasis should be given to take up
 programmes in a comprehensive and an integrated manner for the benefit of women in remote areas such as islands, hilly
 regions and desert areas.  The Committee notes with satisfaction that the first ever biotechnology park for women established in
 Chennai in 1998 has become a huge success. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department may take initiatives
 to establish more such parks in different parts of the country for the benefit of women and society at large.
(Para 35)
Action taken by the Department
Under the activities of National Bioresource development Board of the department, a biotechnology complex for
 capacity building and economic upliftment with particular reference to women of the Indian Himalayan region has been
 established at the old campus of G.B. Pant Institute of Himalayan Environment and Development, Kosi-Katarmal, Almora.
 Under this project, relevant technologies are being demonstrated in selected farmer’s fields. Demonstrations of bio-compost,
 vermicompost, biofertilisers, protected cultivation, fish farming, water harvesting, cultivation of medicinal and aromatic plants,
 mushroom cultivation, biofencing, biobriquetting etc. have been set up in the complex.
            Further, the department has initiated a new scheme namely “Technology Incubators Pilot Level Facilities and Biotech
 Parks” introduced particularly for promotion of biotechnology parks and incubators in the States. A Biotechnology park has
 been established in Lucknow with implementation of Phase-I activities on Bioinformatics. Proposals from other states: Madhya
 Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Rajasthan, Harayana, Gujarat, Orissa, North Eastern States and Himachal
 Pradesh etc. are also at various stages of development.
Comments
The Committee commends the efforts taken by the Department for setting up of biotechnology complexes and parks that
 will make important contributions for the betterment of women’s life particularly in hilly regions and desert areas.
HUMAN GENETICS
Recommendation
The Committee commends the efforts made by the Department to provide molecular diagnosis and counseling for the
 common genetic disorders prevalent in the country.  The Committee recommends that the Department may provide wide
 publicity to the programme through print as well as electronic media  so that the benefits of these activities of the Department
 could percolate to the underprivileged and weaker sections of society.
(Para 38)
Action taken by the Department

In order to reduce the common genetic disorders prevalent in the country, the department of biotechnology has
 established 16 genetic units to provide genetic diagnosis cum counseling to the affected families. So far, about 18039 affected
 families benefited from these units.

 Vivekananda Institute of medical Sciences, Kolkata; Nagpur Medical College, Nagpur; Guru Nanak Dev Univesity, Amritsar;
 Christian Medical College & Hospital, Vellore conducted several public awareness programmes in rural areas and also printed
 brochures in regional languages informing about prevention of common genetic disorders such as thalassemia, muscular
 dystrophy, sickle cell anemia, haemophilia etc. and available diagnostic facilities including prenatal diagnosis and counseling to
 the affected families. Such efforts to provide wide publicity at other centres are also initiated.
Comments: The Committee expresses its satisfaction with the Department’s efforts in creating public awareness as well as
 establishing genetic units in various parts of the country; and hopes that it would cater to the needs of the average citizens.
 
SERI-BIOTECHNOLOGY
Recommendation
The Committee feels that the country has the advantage of production of all four commercial silk varieties viz., mulberry,
 tusser, eri and muga.  The committee notes with satisfaction that the Department is according priority on Seri Biotechnology
 with special focus on non-mulberry silk.  It is heartening for the Committee to know that the Indian Institute of Science,
 Bangalore has, for the first time, done the important job of adopting control measures for pests of silk worm.  As sericulture is
 suitable for marginal, small and landless farmers, it has tremendous scope for expansion in view of its employment generation
 potential. Efforts should, therefore, be made to strengthen the linkages between extension and R&D units.  The technology
 delivery systems should be streamlined by providing need based training and effective field demonstration.  Various
 communication channels should also be used to disseminate information about the new measures to improve to safeguard the
 rights of those who develop it.
(Para 40)
Action taken by the Department
The Department is actively interacting and co-ordinating with Central Silk Board (CSB) with a view to strengthen the
 linkage between user agencies and R&D institutions. Field demonstration projects have also been carried out jointly with CSB
 to disseminate the technology packages for controlling the major diseases/pest of silkworm towards improving the silk yield.
 Training programmes were also an integral part of such demonstrations at the field level. Representatives of CSB have been
 closely associated with the monitoring, review and implementation of the project, supported by DBT in this area.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
MICROBIAL AND INDUSTRIAL BIOTECHNOLOGY
Recommendation
The Committee recommends that the technology developed at the laboratory stage under the programme should be
 brought to the level of pilot plant scale and should be transferred to the industry.  Moreover, the technology developed should
 be patented so as safeguard the rights of those who develop it.
(Para 43)
Action taken by the Department
The department has established sophisticated biotech facilities for scale-up and validation of technologies available at
 laboratory stage. Further, adequate mechanisms have been evolved for the purpose through public- private partnerships and
 technology transfer. Major thrust of the department is to convert research leads into products and processes through technology
 transfer and commercialization involving industry. About 51 technologies from R&D leads transferred to industry and products
 such as HIV diagnostic kits, drug delivery system, Leprosy vaccine (1
st of its kind in the world), 14 diagnostic kits for detection
 of Pregnancy and contraceptive problems, packages for bio-remediation of petroleum oil spills, several bio-fertilizers, bio-
pesticides formulations are already in the market resulting in import substitution and value addition. A patent facilitation cell has
 been established to promote national and international patents of indigenous innovations. So far, 112 patents have been filled
 and 7 International patents and 6 National patents have been granted. To facilitate technology transfer, Biotechnology
 Consortium India Limited (BCIL) is also actively involved.
Comments
The Committee notes with satisfaction the attempts to transfer and commercialize biotech products and processes for use
 in industry.

The Committee also recommends that some new projects in the area of microbial and industrial biotechnology should be
 started with emphasis on development of novel molecules for application in the pharmaceutical and industrial sectors.

The Task Force on Biotech Products and Process Development was apprised to take up new projects in the area of

The Committee commends the progress made by the Task Force on biotech Products and process development.

The Committee feels that the steps taken for facilitating filing of patents at the midway state of producing a product merit

Recommendation
The Committee notes that biotechnology holds the key to food security as well as farmers’ security.  Therefore, the
 Committee recommends that the on-going and new initiatives concerning food biotechnology may be further augmented.  It
 notes with satisfaction that the Department has developed a food which is so nutritious that One kg. of food is equivalent to 5
 kg. of normal food.  While producing more such foods, care must be taken to make the price affordable.  The Committee
 understands that the technology for such foods is transferred to industry and, therefore, it is all the more important to remain
 vigilant about keeping the price of such products affordable.
(Para 47)
Action taken by the Department
The department is already augmenting R&D in the Food Biotechnology area. A mission mode programme on Food and
 Nutritional Security has also been initiated. The endeavors are to minimize the processing costs through biotechnological
 approaches, so that the foods are affordable by the masses.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply with satisfaction.

Recommendation
The Committee observes that the National Institute of Immunology (NII) should also take steps to focus its research
 activities on certain unexplored areas in the field of Immunodiagnostics.
(Para 52)
Recommendation
The Committee also recommends that the Department may explore the possibility of raising funds by collaborating with
 the industry for providing additional support to research activities.  It will open opportunities for making the Institute self-
sufficient.
(Para 53)

The National Brain Research Centre, an autonomous institution of the Department of Biotechnology, through its
 networking with 42 institutions has helped to promote neuroscience in the country. Multi-institutional collaboration projects are
 operational with other premier institutions in the country such as Indian Institute of Sciences (IISc.), & National Institute of
 Mental Health & Neuroscience (NIMHANS), Bangalore,; Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Kanpur ; All India Institute of
 Medical Sciences (AIIMS) & Institute of Genomic and Integrative Biology (IGIB), New  Delhi etc. The institute has played a
 very important role in revitalizing brain research in the country and initiating modern neuroscience research that is highly
 integrative and multidisciplinary. Several workshops, particularly those in computational neuroscience are conducted
 periodically in association with National Centre for Biological Sciences, Bangalore and IIT (Delhi) and IIT (Kanpur) for
 awareness among scientists and industry.

The Committee commends various projects and workshops undertaken by the department towards the promotion of

The Committee endorses the vision of the Department to make agriculture sustainable by using biotechnology.  To get
 better yields, we need plants and methods of cultivation which will be in harmony with biodiversity and eco-system and,
 therefore, will not bring down the fertility of land and kill useful animals, pests and weeds.  This objective can be achieved by,
 among others, changing plant characteristics through genetic modification.  The Committee impresses upon the Department to
 work with full vigour to realise this objective.  Prof. M.S. Swaminathan, one of the leading figures who spearheaded green
 revolution in our country, has said that green revolution can become ever green revolution by making it pro-nature, pro-poor
 and pro-women.  Therefore, the Committee emphasizes that the Department while focusing on biotechnology should also
 harness social forces for making our agriculture sustainable.
(Para 68)
Action Taken by the Department
 Biotechnology interventions have the potential to enhance the yield level, increase resistance/tolerance to biotic and
 abiotic stresses, reduce pesticide use thereby making cultivation of crops eco-friendly and improve nutritional quality.  The
 department has supported a major multi-institutional project on development of transgenic crops (rice, cotton, mungbean and
 tomato) resistant to biotic stresses.  Similarly, some R&D projects are also being supported in this direction.  Another project on
 salinity and dehydration stress tolerance in rice has been supported recently. The project would ultimately result in raising of
 rice transgenic employing candidate genes for resistance against salinity/dehydrations stress.   In an attempt to solve the
 problem of malnutrition in rural areas, a multi-institutional coordinated programme to enhance quantity/quality of protein and
 micronutrients in important food crops viz. rice, cassava and sweet potato has also been supported.
Comments
The Committee notes with satisfaction Biotechnology based projects towards making agriculture sustainable and hopes 
 that awareness will be generated among the rural masses for popularizing such projects.
EXPEDITIOUS CLEARANCE OF PROJECTS SUBMITTED BY THE DEPARTMENT
Recommendation
The Committee was apprised that the proposals submitted by the Department are subjected to periodic review and
 assessment by different agencies including the Planning Commission. The Department further stated that it remained ever ready
 to subject itself and its activities to scrutiny.  However, it informed the Committee that time taken for review of its projects is
 too long and, therefore, comes in the way of its expeditious implementation.  While pursuing research in the field of science, the
 Department has to constantly innovate to remain abreast of the ever-evolving activities of the scientific community across the
 globe.  Delay in clearing a project, therefore, will throw a spanner in the wheel of scientific progress which the Department is
 carrying forward within a limited budget, to fulfill the objectives set before them in a goal oriented and time bound manner. 
 Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that all the proposals of the Department must be cleared expeditiously and
 within a set time frame.
(Para 76)
Action Taken by the Department
The issues related to clearing of projects by other departments and Planning Commission have been taken up at highest
 level and the same has been streamlined.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply with satisfaction and further suggests that the Department should pursue the matter with
 the highest decision-making body so that the objectives of clearing of various projects can be achieved with an immediate
 effect.
BUDGET PROPOSALS AT REVISED ESTIMATES STAGE
Recommendation
The Department informed the Committee that the reduction of its budget at the R.E. stage causes a lot of problem in
 resetting its priorities.  It prepares its plan as per the budget proposals and accordingly prepares its schedule of activities.  Time
 taken to re-do the priorities due to cut in R.E. stage is not less than three or four months.  Such re-planning for scientific projects
 deviates the Department from the set objectives.  The Committee is constrained to note that such problems are confronted by the
 Department.
Prof. G. Padmanabhan, the UNESCO Professor in Biotechnology, Department of  Biochemistry, Indian Institute of
 Science, Bangalore in an important article “Contrary to reports, India has not missed the biotech bus” has written about
 the budget requirements of biotechnology which is revealing:
“ A single funding agency in the USA has a Rs.4,000 crores budget for genomics.  In India, all the funding agencies
 together can mobilize about Rs.100 crores a year to research in this area.  It is interesting to note that the country can
 still come up with new drugs, vaccines and diagnostics within this limited budget.  If India plays its cards right, it can

 hope to become a world leader in modern vaccine manufacturing, since MNCs are not interested in this field due to poor
 economic returns.  All that is needed is a commitment on the part of the Government to ensure availability of the
 committed amount for the next five years, release of grants in time, a mechanism for quick clearance of clinical trials to

(Para 77)
Recommendation
Determination and will of the scientists to achieve the goal which is comparable to international standards and within a
 limited but committed fund is indeed heartening.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the budgets for all the
 Departments dealing with science and technology including that of the Department of Biotechnology may not be reduced at the
 R.E. stage.
(Para 78)

The matter is being pursued with Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

The Committee notes the replies.
USE OF TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE
Recommendation
India is rich with traditional knowledge.  Our people with centuries of experiences have emerged as practitioners of such
 knowledge.  This rich reservoir of such resources must be understood scientifically and safeguarded.  The Committee was
 informed by a Member that Ganga Jal, Gou Mutra and Gober have anti-bacterial properties.  It was also told that Gober is
 radiation resistant.  It was told that when hospital wastes were treated with layers of Gober for five months, it was found that all
 bacteria, toxin and poison had been neutralised.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that steps must be taken by the
 Department to explore the anti-bacterial properties of Ganga Jal, Gou Mutra and Gober, specially the effectiveness for treating
 hospital waste.
(Para 79)
Action Taken by the Department
The Department has noted the recommendations of the Committee on Ganga Jal, Gou Mutra and Gobar. At present, there
 are no specific projects in these areas. However, other agencies like Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) have
 conducted investigations and experimentations on the utilities of the above-mentioned products. Similarly, Ministry of Health &
 Family Welfare and Ministry of Environment and Forest are implementing projects/programmes on regulation and treatment of
 hospital waste in which the department is not directly involved. However, in future, if any such proposal is submitted to the
 department, it will be considered on scientific merit.
Comments
        The Committee feels that the department should initiate efforts on its own with regard to exploring the anti-bacterial
 properties of Ganga Jal, Gou Mutra and Gobar.

 R E P O R T
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Space on the recommendations
 contained in the One Hundred-fourteenth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science &
 Technology, Environment & Forests on the Demands for Grants (2003-2004) of the Department of Space which was presented
 to both Houses of Parliament on 2 nd May, 2003.  There were twenty-one recommendations contained in One Hundred-
fourteenth Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the
 Department on 5th September, 2003.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the              Committee on the action taken by
 the Department of Space are set out in the succeeding paragraphs: -
INSAT SERIES
Recommendation
The Committee congratulates the Department for the successful launch of the INSAT-3A and records its appreciation for
 the abilities and talents of our scientists who have further enhanced the glory of our nation through this splendid performance.
 The Committee hopes that the other satellites in the INSAT series would be launched as planned without any cost escalation.
(Para 24)
Action Taken by the Department
After the launch of INSAT-3A on April 10, 2003, the spacecraft has been commissioned in orbit and put to operational
 use. The next satellite, INSAT-3E, is also now ready for launch. The spacecraft has been transported to the launch site French
 Guyana and the launch is scheduled for the third quarter of 2003. The work on INSAT -3D, an advanced meteorological
 satellite and also the last satellite in the INSAT -3 series, is in progress and the launch is targeted for 2004-05 onboard India's
 GSLV. The work on fourth generation INSAT-4A & 4B satellites has also begun. No cost escalation is foreseen in INSAT
 satellites at present.
 
Also, GSAT-2, an experimental communication satellite, was successfully launched on the second developmental flight
 of GSLV (GSLV-D2) on May 8, 2003 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota. GSAT-2 has augmented the INSAT
 capacity with four C-band, two Ku band and One Mobile Satellite Service transponders.
Comments
The Committee congratulates the Department of Space and scientists of ISRO for the successful launch of GSAT-2 and
 expresses its best wishes for the success of all the future programmes.
DEVELOPMENT OF CRYOGENIC ENGINES
Proven abilities of our scientists have now to be used to develop the cryogenic technology which has been subjected to
 many experiments. The Committee feels that the indigenous development of cryogenic engines is critical to the development of
 our own geostationary satellite launch vehicles. It express full faith on our space scientists and hopes that they will accomplish
 the mission.

Action Taken by the Department
ISRO has made considerable progress related to the development of our indigenous cryogenic stage for use on Geo-
synchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV). The first two-engine hardware have undergone a total cumulative ground hot test
 firing duration of 4000 seconds. These tests have given confidence for the normal performance of the engine. Preparation for
 the stage test is in progress and stage tankages have been moved to the test stand for various tests before conducting the first hot
 test planned this year. The first set of flight version tanks have been realized. Based on a success-oriented schedule, it is planned
 to make a test flight of the indigenous cryogenic stage during 2004-05. The work on development of a higher thrust cryogenic
 engine (C-25) has also been initiated as a part of GSLV Mk III project.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the progress in the development of the indigenous cryogenic engines. However, it hopes that
 the progress in the development of higher thrust cryogenic engines (C-25) would be initiated as per schedule so that the projects
 like Mission to Moon, envisaged with cryogenic engines are not delayed.
GRAMSAT PILOT PROJECTS (GPP)
Recommendation
The Committee hopes that by the end of the 10
th Plan period the GRAMSAT programme would cover all the rural areas
 of India. The Committee also hopes that local bodies, district offices and all those involved in planning at the rural level would
 be given the data for their use. Since we have constitutionally guaranteed 33% reservation for women in Panchayat bodies, the
 Committee recommends that special focus should be given to women's development issues through GRAMSAT. Lest all this
 effort goes waste the Committee strongly urges the government to launch a scheme to equip every village of the country with
 the equipment necessary to utilize the service that will be given through GRAMSAT.
(Para 38)
Action Taken by the Department
GRAMSAT programme envisages provision of satellite transponders for developmental communications including
 education and training, health, women & child development, Panchayati Raj functionaries etc. Under GRAMSAT Pilot Projects,
 such networks have already been established in Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Orissa, Goa and
 Rajasthan. The developmental programmes broadcasted under the network by State Governments address the women
 development issues also. In fact, the impact evaluation of the GRAMSAT network in Jhabua district of Madhya Pradesh
 indicates that the backward and tribal communities of the region, especially women are the main beneficiaries of the
 GRAMSAT programme. Work has already been initiated to build a satellite - EDUSAT (GSAT-3) -dedicated for spreading
 education and training at all levels covering a large area of the country including North East through a satellite based network.
Comments
The Committee observes that steps may be taken to cover all the states, particularly the hill states by the next phase of
 GRAMSAT project and hopes that EDUSAT satellite would cover wider regions.
LAUNCH VEHICLE INFRASTRUCTURE
Recommendation
The Committee commends the Department for making significant progress in completion of second launch pad and
 hopes that it would be ready for commissioning by the end of this year without any further delays.
(Para 40)
Action Taken by the Department
The Second Launch Pad is now ready to receive PSLV and the activities related to mock-up trials have been initiated.
 The Second Launch pad will be ready to receive     GSLV by end of the year after completing the installation and
 commissioning of           Cryo processing facilities.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the second launch pad would reduce our  dependence on foreign launching pads and besides,
 India could  offer its launching services to other countries.

Recommendation
The Committee hopes that the ISRO-GEO sphere programme would be helpful in predicting, the arrival of monsoon with

ISRO-GBP focuses on the issues related to characterisation of parameters responsible for climate change. The

SPONSORED RESEARCH
Recommendation
The committee recommends that apart from initiating the research projects in the academic institutions, the Department
 should develop a mechanism for constant monitoring of the performance of the projects to ensure their timely completion.
(Para 56)
Action Taken by the Department
The ISRO Sponsored Research Projects (RESPOND) are carried out at the Academic Institutions such as Universities,
 Colleges, National Institutions, IITs, Research laboratories under the supervision of experts at ISRO Centres. The Department
 has established a well-structured review system as below to monitor the progress of these research projects.
(a)        Each project has been assigned with a Focal Point (Expert) from the ISRO Centre who will interact with the
 project on a timely basis to ensure smooth progress of the project work. At the end of every year, the project
 submits an annual progress report which is reviewed by the Focal Point and other experts at ISRO Centres before
 recommending further renewal (continuation) of the project and release of grants for the next year.
(b)        Since last 5 years, ISRO has initiated an additional review mechanism, the Annual RESPOND Review meetings
 at ISRO Centres, where an exclusive ISRO Committee constituted and chaired by Director of each ISRO Centre
 will review the progress of the Projects and make suitable suggestions and mid-course corrections on the project
 work to ensure satisfactory completion of the project within the project period.
Comments
The Committee notes with satisfaction the initiatives taken by the Department for  review of the progress of  sponsored
 research projects.
 
TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER
Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Department for transfer of technologies to the Industry; however, the
 Committee recommends that the Department should acquire patents of the technologies transferred to prevent exploitation. The
 Department should assess such technology transfers from the commercial point of view and generate the maximum revenue out
 of it. The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Department is bringing in more and more participation from industry in
 conducting the space programme. The Committee hopes that through greater transfer of technology, participation of industry
 will be further broadened.
(Para 62)
Action Taken by the Department
ISRO/DOS has been pursuing a Technology Transfer (TT) policy that has enabled the commercialization of ISRO
 developed technologies through Indian industries. Adequate measures are being taken to safeguard ISRO's interest through
 filing of appropriate patents, copyrights and trademarks. The technology transfer mechanism established by ISRO has resulted
 in more than 255 technologies being  licensed to the Indian industries in the small, medium and large scale sectors. Efforts are
 being made to widen the avenues and scope for industry participation with a view to maximally utilize the industrial capability
 and expertise.

INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION
Marketing of Space Services & Products
Recommendation
The Committee feels that India's expertise in space technology can be further shared with many other developing
 countries. The Department should explore opportunities for launching of more satellites and marketing of remote sensing data to
 many other countries.
(Para. 73)
Action Taken by the Department
ISRO has set up a Scheme "Sharing of Experience in Space (SHARES)" under which training in different applications of
 space science, technology and applications is provided to scientists from developing countries. Another important initiative in
 this direction is the establishment of the Centre for Space Science and Technology Education for Asia and the Pacific (CSSTE-
AP) affiliated to United Nations which offers specialized training in Remote Sensing & Geographical Information System,
 Satellite Communications, Satellite Meteorology, Global climate & Space / Atmospheric Studies and more than 300 scholars
 from about 40 developing countries have been benefited from this Centre.
The Department through Antrix Corporation (ANTRIX), the commercial wing of the Department of Space has mounted
 efforts towards promoting the market for launch services and marketing of remote sensing data to global customers. Concerted
 efforts have been made by contacting a number of potential customers in Europe (Germany, Sweden, Italy etc.), Canada etc., for
 provision of launch services, though the geo-political constraints play a dominant role in the global launch services market. On
 the marketing of remote sensing data, discussions have been held with international customers in South Africa, Yemen, Ecuador
 and Algeria etc., for the reception and dissemination of IRS data. Efforts are also on to provide value added services to
 Mauritius in the area of land Information System (LIS). Preliminary proposals have been submitted to the customer in this
 regard.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Development of low cost technologies 
Recommendation
The Committee feels that intense competition is on to capture the limited market of space industry and India can innovate
 design concepts for small as well as large payloads and by doing so can offer competitive prices to the interested countries for
 availing of India's technologies. The Committee recommends that the Department may explore the possibility of developing low
 cost space technologies which would be useful to developing countries.
(Para 74)
Action Taken by the Department
The Department with its unique expertise in space application, spacecraft and launching has been exploring the
 possibility of end-to-end services, which can be useful to developing nations.
With the GSLV capability improving to launch satellites of weight higher than 2000 kg; Department of Space is planning
 to launch satellites compatible with indigenous launchers and catering to the emerging markets such as DTH, TV broadcasting,
 long distance thin route communications, Ku-band satellites with multiple beams, Ka- band Regenerative payload etc. are being
 planned to develop low-cost space technologies suited to developing countries, Discussions are under way for providing
 satellite based communication systems for Vietnam, Malaysia etc.
Further, the concept of developing micro-satellites with appropriate payloads has been developed along with the Anna
 University, which also provides opportunities to develop low cost based technologies that could be of relevance and use to the
 developing countries.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

 geography, distance, time and costs. It believes that this can be a boon for countries like India where the majority population

Telemedicine Kiosks
Recommendation
The Committee also hopes that in the next few years there will be telemedicine kiosks through the length and breadth of
 suburban and rural India. It is hoped that the government scheme to provide such kiosks will go hand in hand with the spread of
 telemedicine facility.
(Para 78)
Action Taken by the Department
The telemedicine technology demonstration projects have been operating in the State of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh,
 Kerala, UT of Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands, Jammu & Kashmir including Ladakh, Assam, Sikkim and
 Tripura etc., connecting 27 hospitals (10 super speciality hospitals, 17 district/medical college hospitals) providing specialist
 consultation to remote hospitals located at rural and inaccessible areas.
The telemedicine system consists of customized medical software integrated with the diagnostic instruments like EGG,
 X-ray scanner which will be connected to VSAT for connectivity with the satellite. Similar VSAT and the medical software
 exists at the specialist end for viewing and analysis of the medical information. The tele-consultation and treatment are provided
 during the video conferencing between the patient end hospital and the specialist end.
The concept of a Tele-medicine Kiosk co-located with Information Kiosks can provide only limited Tele-medicine
 services out of different alternatives. Appropriate option in terms of technology, location, etc., which would maximize the Tele-
 medicine benefits to the remote areas will have to be adopted by implementing agencies.
Comments 
The Committee appreciates the Department’s projects under telemedicine system and feels that by expanding
 telemedicine facilities the objective of access to health care could be realized. The big hospitals in the States of Uttar Pradesh,
 Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Orissa and Bihar should also be linked with telemedicine projects as maximum poor people are
 living in these States.
 
 
DISASTER MANAGEMENT SUPPORT (DMS)
Recommendation
The committee feels that the remote sensing data is not being used to its full potential. With regard, to the landslide
 hazard zonation, the Committee feels that standardized landslide inventory maps would be helpful. Besides, accurate slop
 stability studies may be made by using space technology so as to understand the possible locations where landslides could
 occur. The Committee feels that special attention should be given to Northeast and Uttaranchal where landslides during rainy
 season block roads for days together. An Internet image transferring system may be of help for local bodies and relief agencies
 for emergency response in affected areas.
(Para 87)
Action Taken by the Department
Remote sensing data usage is coordinated under the auspices of the National Natural Resources Management System
 (NNRMS) with active involvement of various Central/State agencies as well as private entrepreneurs and academia. India is one
 of the very few countries in the world, which has effectively integrated remote sensing applications with developmental
 planning at various levels. However, considering that it is still a continuing process and there are newer applications and
 services in the light of advancement in technologies, the Department continues to spread the awareness through appropriate
 training and education programmes, which should enable further enhancement of remote sensing data usage in the future.
Initiatives have already been taken on landslide hazard zonation studies in the North East and the Uttaranchal. A network
 based information transfer and access system towards helping local bodies and relief agencies for emergency response in
 affected areas is being worked out.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

 NATIONAL NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (NNRMS)
Recommendation
The Committee is of the opinion that a periodic census of the available natural resources would help assessing the
 utilization of such resources so as to formulate a plan for sustainable development.
(Para 91)
Action Taken by the Department
The NNRMS has identified the conduct of a Natural Resource Census (NRC) in the country as a major national activity
 from 10th Plan onwards. As pre-investment activity for the National Mission of NRC, a proto-type exercise has been taken up
 in 12 districts of the country. The Proto-type will generate national mapping standards for NRC and also help operationalise the
 mechanisms of the national mission. After completing the Proto-type activity during the year, the national programme on NRC
 will be initiated.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the National Mission on NRC would be taken up in all the districts of the country so that
 realistic census on the natural resources is drawn up for effective development planning.
NORTH EAST SPACE APPLICATION CENTRE
Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the Department for undertaking projects in the Northeast, which merits concentrated
 attention. The Committee hopes that bamboo resource mapping, erosion hazard assessment etc. would cover the whole of the
 Northeast so that the data could be used for meaningful planning for development.
(Para 93)
Action Taken by the Department
The Department through its North Eastern Space Applications Centre (NE- SAC) has initiated many remote sensing
 application projects covering the whole North East for providing inputs for developmental planning of the region.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the inputs provided by North East Space Application Centre would help in finalizing projects
 for industrial and agricultural development of the region.
Ground Water exploration
Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that India is emerging as a water stressed country with millions of its people without
 access to safe drinking water. The Committee deeply appreciates that the Department has applied Space Technology to prepare
 1500 maps in respect of six States for the purpose of ground water exploration. While the Committee notes that the Department
 is mapping for few of the States, it recommends strongly that such efforts of the Department must be extended to all States,
 giving special priority to those, which have been severely affected by drought and shortage of rainfall.
(Para 94)
Action Taken by the Department
The Department has been working with the Department of Drinking Water Supply (Ministry of Rural Development),
 Government of India towards providing inputs to the Rajiv Gandhi National Drinking Water Mission (RGNDWM) for the
 purpose of ground water exploration as well as recharge. The Department will work closely with the RGNDW to extend the
 above activities to other States as suggested.
Comments
The Committee would like the Department to evolve an effective monitoring mechanism with Department of Drinking
 Water Supply (Ministry of Rural Development) to see the programme succeeds.
National Resource Information Systems
Recommendation
The Committee notes that the Department is proposing to prepare National Resource Information System in Nine States.
 Earlier the Department had set up such a system in 30 districts in different States. The Committee recommends that such
 systems be established as soon as possible in all the States of the country to enable the Government, people and larger civil
 society to have access to such information for national development.
(Para 95)
